topics.title: Log a reading
topics.sub: Vitals, pain, a drink, food, a note, sleep, bowels, a symptom or how you feel, from Today.
topics.intro: Everything between the check-ins is logged from the tiles on Today, in the same way.

steps.caption: On Today, tap Vitals. The other tiles log pain, a drink, food, a note, sleep, bowels, a symptom or your mood the same way.
Type the readings you have. Any box can be left empty, and the time is filled in for you.
37.6 and 97 typed. For a reading taken earlier, change the time or the date, then tap Save.
Saved. It is on the timeline for the day, coloured if it is raised, and the Reports charts have it too. The three dots on an entry edit or delete it.

topics.title: The morning and evening check-ins
topics.sub: A minute each: sleep, symptoms, pain and mood, one question a screen.
topics.intro: The check-ins are what the reports are built from. A minute each, twice a day.

steps.caption: Twice a day, a morning check-in and an evening one. Tap the row when it says Due now.
One question a screen. Slide to the score, then when you went to bed and woke up: Daybook works out the hours. With Apple Health connected, the night fills itself in.
Rested, and whether the night was broken: if it was, what broke it and roughly for how long. It goes on the Sleep chart and the reports.
A written answer has Tap to speak under it: tap, say it, tap again to stop. To see what was heard before it is saved, switch that on in Settings. Skip is always there.
Pain right now, from 0 no pain to 10 worst imaginable: as you slide it says mild, moderate or severe. Where it is goes in the box underneath.
The review: every answer, tap one to change it, then Save.
Done. The check-in is a card on Today: tap it to open it, and Edit to change an answer later.

topics.title: Medicines and reminders
topics.sub: Log a dose, see what is due, set reminder times.
topics.intro: Every dose is logged on the Meds tab: Log now, or Other time for a dose taken earlier.

steps.caption: The Meds tab lists today's medicines, each with how many doses are done. Tap Log now when one is taken.
Logged: the line counts it, and the name opens the card with the time of each dose, Other time, Remove and Log a side effect. A when-needed medicine says when the next dose can be given.
The arrows at the foot of an open card, or holding the name for a second and sliding it, put the list in your own order.
Manage medicines adds one, changes a dose or the times it is taken. Reminders arrive as notifications once they are switched on under Settings.
Add a medicine sits at the top. Under it, every medicine on the list, with what it is for and Edit. A finished course keeps its history under Medicine history.
Edit says whether it is regular or when needed, then how it is taken (tablets, gel in pumps and the rest), how many each time and the strength, so Log now records the right amount.
A regular medicine then asks when you take it: tick Morning, Midday, Teatime or Night and set each time. One in the morning and one at night is Morning and Night. The same times are its reminders.

topics.title: A question for the team
topics.sub: Keep the questions for the next appointment, labelled for who answers them.
topics.intro: A question written down when it comes to you is a question that gets asked.

steps.caption: Something to ask at the next appointment? Tap Question for the team on Today.
Type it, or Tap to speak, and say who it is for: Oncology, Gastro, General, Dietitian, Wellbeing or the Pain team. It goes to the top of that report.
Saved. The row now says how many are waiting; tap it to see them all.
Every question still waiting, from any date. Mark one as answered once the team has dealt with it, or add another at the foot.
Every open question heads Notes for the team, with room under it for the answer in clinic. Record or write the answer, then mark it answered.

topics.title: Treatment days and side effects
topics.sub: The calendar, where you are in the cycle, and how the days after a session went.
topics.intro: The Treatment tab holds the sessions, the days after them, and how each cycle tends to go.

steps.caption: The Treatment tab: the next session at the top, then the calendar. Sessions carry a letter, C for chemo, and turn gold once ticked done.
Add sessions puts a whole run in at once: the first date, how many and how often. A session that moves is moved from its own day.
Tap a day after a session to see how it went: the side effects rated in that day's check-ins, your own words, and anything logged.
On the three days after a session, the morning and evening check-ins ask about side effects: none, mild, moderate or severe for each.
How treatment goes: energy, sickness, appetite, pain, mood or sleep by day after each session, so the shape of a cycle shows after a few.

topics.title: Your week
topics.sub: Five minutes, once a week, over the last days of your week.
topics.intro: The weekly check is what the Mood and wellbeing report builds its weeks from.

steps.caption: Over the last three days of the week, Your week appears on Today: five minutes, once a week.
Four words for each question, then three boxes in your own words. Every tap is saved as you go.
Finish when it is done. Close it instead and Today says it is not finished yet, with everything kept.
Done for the week. Tap the row again to change an answer.
The week ends on Sunday unless you change it under More, Settings, Your week. With treatment on the calendar, one tap makes it end on your treatment day.

topics.title: Reports, and emailing them
topics.sub: Notes for the team, the Food diary, Mood and wellbeing, Pain, and the charts.
topics.intro: Each report is a page or two for one person on the team, made from what is already logged.

steps.caption: The Reports tab: Notes for the team first, then the Food diary, Mood and wellbeing, Pain and pain relief, Documents, and the charts of every reading.
Choose the period, then Send to the team, Preview or Save as PDF. The summary and the notes are below.
Pick who it goes to. Contacts with an email address come from Who to contact on More.
The subject and message are written for you and can be changed. The report is attached as a PDF, and a copy goes to your own inbox.
Preview shows the pages exactly as they print. Pinch, double tap, or use plus and minus to zoom in on the report alone. Print and Save as PDF are above.

topics.title: Pain, food and mood reports
topics.sub: A report for the pain team, the dietitian, and whoever helps with how you feel.
topics.intro: Each report is made for one reader, from what is already logged.

steps.caption: Beside Notes for the team: Pain and pain relief for the pain team, the Food diary for the dietitian, Mood and wellbeing for a therapist or GP.

Pain and pain relief: two weeks to start, the check-in scores, the worst each day, key points from what you wrote, every dose of pain relief and when the top-ups were taken. Send, Preview and Save as PDF, as on every report.
The Food diary: what was eaten and drunk each day, with the questions for the dietitian, on two pages.
Mood and wellbeing: the best and hardest days, how often you felt low, sleep and pain behind it, and the weeks, with a carer's view in its own area.

topics.title: Crohn's or colitis
topics.sub: Bowels, flares, injections, results and the report for the IBD team.
topics.intro: With Crohn's or colitis ticked in Settings, Daybook adds what an IBD team asks about.

steps.caption: With Crohn's or colitis set up, Today has I think I'm flaring under the check-ins.
A 7-day summary to read out or send to the advice line, what the team told you to do in their own words, and a log of your calls.
Bowels logs each movement in a few taps.
The seven stool types as rows, hard to watery, then any blood and how long you could wait. Tap every type in a mixed one.
The morning check-in asks whether you are fasting today, and which kind. One tap; it goes on the Food diary and the reports.
The Treatment tab: your flare plan, flare days shaded on the calendar, injections or infusions with the next one due, and any steroid course.
Results: blood tests and calprotectin as the team gave them, charted against the lab's own range. Daybook never says whether one is good or bad.
The Crohn's and colitis report: bowels against your usual, blood, urgency, flares, treatment and results, with your questions for the gastro team.

topics.title: Who to contact, and the set-up
topics.sub: The ward, the nurse, the GP: one tap to call or email, and where the reports go.
topics.intro: More holds the Set-up, this Guide, letters and paperwork, saved meals, Settings and Who to contact.

steps.caption: More: the Set-up, the Guide, letters and paperwork, saved meals, Settings, and Who to contact. Tap Add a new contact.
A name, and a phone number or an email address, or both. Save.
Call and Email are one tap. Any contact with an email address can be sent a report from the Reports tab.
The Set-up: what Daybook is for, your name on the reports, a contact, the Home Screen and Tap to speak. Run it again any time, from here or from Settings.

topics.title: A carer's phone
topics.sub: Invited as a carer: the same Daybook, with your own view of their mood, the week and the day.
topics.intro: Someone invited as a carer logs and reads everything the same way, and adds their own view alongside.

steps.caption: A carer's Today has two more rows: their mood this morning and this evening, as you see it, at the patient's own times.
Their mood on 1 to 10, then anything you noticed. It goes on the timeline and the Mood and wellbeing report, never mixed with the patient's own scores.
Over the last days of the week, Your week, as you see it: how the patient seemed, kept apart from their own answers.
Four questions on how they seemed this week, then three in your own words. It goes on Notes for the team and the Mood and wellbeing report as "As Shelley saw it".

topics.title: From the day to the report
topics.sub: A day's logging, a question when it comes to you, then two pages for the team, sent from the app.
topics.intro: This is what Daybook is for: the days between appointments, logged as they happen, become the report for the next one.

steps.caption: A day starts on Today. The morning check-in is due: a minute, one question a screen.
How you slept, anything new overnight, pain and mood. Slide to the score, or Tap to speak for the words.
Saved as a card. Through the day the tiles log a drink, a meal, how you feel, a symptom or a bowel movement in a few taps.
The Mood tile logs how you feel right now, between the check-ins. Doses are logged on the Meds tab.
A question comes to you at 3am. Write it down and it waits for the appointment.
Say who it is for, and it goes to the top of that team's report.
Before the appointment, open Reports. Everything since the last one is already there.
Notes for the team: the questions, what changed, the charts and the week's notes, on two pages. Preview shows them as they print.
Two A4 pages the team can read in a minute, with room to write. Print them, or send them from the app.
Send to the team emails the PDF to the nurse, the dietitian or the oncologist, with a copy to you. One tap, and it is done.
